newsitem.title: PERU: Peru decrees 63 percent increase in minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: Peru decrees 63 percent increase in minimum wage.

text.p: The Peruvian government decreed Tuesday a 63 percent increase in workers' minimum wage to 215 soles ($86) a month from 132 soles a month.

The decree, published in the government daily El Peruano, also states employees working at night between 2200 local and 0600 should receive a minimum wage 30 percent above the basic 215 soles a month.
The decree "shows the government's concern to improve - as far as is possible - the labor situation in the country," labor minister Jorge Gonzalez Izquierdo said in an interview on local radio.
The decree is part of a package of laws the government is preparing, after Congress granted the executive last week a 30-day extension to its special legislative powers.
